title: ReviewableModuleView Sync toasts 'Imported undefined features'
body:
## Summary
useReviewableModuleView.handleSync reads `imported` off the {success,data} envelope, the twin of the bug fixed in useModuleReviewCli (21f4f6ab).

## Description
/api/feature-matrix/import returns apiSuccess({ imported, ... }) (src/app/api/feature-matrix/import/route.ts:249). src/components/modules/shared/ReviewableModuleView/useReviewableModuleView.ts:269-270 does `const data = await res.json(); toast.success(`Imported ${data.imported} features`)`, so every successful manual Sync in every ReviewableModuleView module says 'Imported undefined features'. Fixed = tryApiFetch<{imported:number}> as in src/hooks/useModuleReviewCli.ts after 21f4f6ab. The file belongs to another context, so this round did not touch it.

## Flow
- Open any module using ReviewableModuleView -> click Sync -> POST /api/feature-matrix/import 200
- toast reads 'Imported undefined features'
- fix: swap raw fetch for tryApiFetch, mirror useModuleReviewCli.sync.test.tsx

## Expected impact
Every operator who syncs a review sees a real count. Could break nothing beyond the toast text.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the sync toast reports the imported count
Before: 1/1 success path toasts 'undefined' (same envelope read as the fixed twin)
After: the twin hook's test went red->green on the same change (21f4f6ab); predicted identical here
Method: simulation - walked the identical code path; the fix lives in another context's file
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: copy src/__tests__/hooks/useModuleReviewCli.sync.test.tsx onto useReviewableModuleView with a toast spy; red on base, green after

title: Adaptive skill packs reach the run only if a telemetry fetch wins a race
body:
## Summary
useModuleCLI.execute fires resolveAndApplySkills as fire-and-forget and dispatches without waiting, so whether skill packs are injected depends on network ordering.

## Description
src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:295 starts the /api/telemetry resolve-skills fetch, then awaits composeTaskDispatch and calls sendPrompt (src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:305-306). Skills are injected at send time from session.enabledSkills (src/components/cli/skills.ts:238-241). If the fetch resolves after the prompt is sent, this run gets no packs; on the first run for a sessionKey the fetch may resolve before sendPrompt creates the session (src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:335 finds no tab) and the packs are dropped entirely. Fixed = await the resolve (bounded by a short timeout) before sendPrompt, or pass the resolved skills in the dispatch.

## Flow
- execute(task) on a fresh sessionKey
- telemetry fetch resolves -> tabOrder has no session -> setSessionSkills skipped
- sendPrompt creates the session with enabledSkills [] -> run has no packs

## Expected impact
Runs get the skill packs their telemetry selected, deterministically. Could add up to the timeout's latency to a dispatch.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - skill injection is deterministic per dispatch
Before: outcome depends on fetch vs composeTaskDispatch ordering (3 orderings walked, 1 injects into this run)
After: predicted: 1 ordering-independent outcome
Method: simulation - three orderings walked (fetch first/new key, fetch first/existing key, fetch last)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: renderHook(useModuleCLI) with deferred fetch mocks for /api/telemetry and the dispatch resolver; assert enabledSkills on the dispatched session under both resolution orders

title: Client callback registry grows by one entry per prompt build, never drained
body:
## Summary
registerCallback adds to a module-level Map on every buildTaskPrompt (dispatches and previews); entries leave only on a successful client resolveCallback, which terminal runs no longer use.

## Description
src/lib/cli-task.ts:52-60 registers; removal only in resolveCallback on success (src/lib/cli-task.ts:282). Terminal runs are settled server-side (src/lib/claude-terminal/run-callbacks.ts), and removeCallback has 0 consumers outside cli-task.ts (grep over src excl. tests). The handlers in src/lib/cli-task-handlers.ts (11+ registerCallback sites) register on every build, including TaskPromptInspector previews. Fixed = bound the Map (LRU cap) or drop entries once useTaskQueue has declared them with the query POST (src/components/cli/useTaskQueue.ts:38).

## Flow
- build N task prompts (previews or dispatches)
- Map size == N for the tab's lifetime

## Expected impact
Bounded memory on long sessions. Could break Resubmit of a very old failed payload if the cap evicts it.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - registry size bounded
Before: entries == number of prompt builds (unbounded); removeCallback consumers: 0
After: predicted: <= cap
Method: simulation - read of the registration/removal sites
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a test that builds 1000 checklist prompts via buildTaskPrompt and asserts the registry size via an exported size() probe, red on base

title: Budget fetch failure renders as 'no limit, $0 spent'
body:
## Summary
useBudget.refetch swallows every error and keeps the empty default, so a failed budget read is indistinguishable from an unconfigured budget.

## Description
src/hooks/useCliSpend.ts:71-76 catches and ignores; the default (src/hooks/useCliSpend.ts:9-20) says no daily/monthly limit and $0 spend. SpendBudgetPanel then shows no limits and empty meters. Fixed = expose an `error` from useBudget and render it in SpendBudgetPanel (src/components/modules/evaluator/SpendBudgetPanel.tsx, another context's file).

## Flow
- /api/cli-spend?action=budget returns 500
- useBudget keeps emptyBudgetStatus
- panel reads 'no limit' with $0 today

## Expected impact
An operator with a configured budget sees that the read failed instead of believing none is set. Breaks nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed budget read is visible
Before: 0 surfaces show the failure (error swallowed)
After: predicted: 1 inline error
Method: simulation - walked the catch path
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/hooks/useCliSpend.ts:73 } catch {
src/hooks/useCliSpend.ts:74 // Non-critical — keep the empty default.
instrument: renderHook(useBudget) with a 500 fetch; assert result.current.error set (red on base); plus a SpendBudgetPanel render asserting the error text

title: Selection toolbar 'Search in project' dispatches an event nobody listens to
body:
## Summary
The terminal selection toolbar's Search button fires `pof-terminal-search` with zero listeners in src or e2e, so it only clears the selection.

## Description
src/components/cli/TerminalOutput/useTerminalOutput.ts dispatches CustomEvent('pof-terminal-search') in handleSelectionSearch; grep for the name over src and e2e finds only the dispatch. The only pof-* window listeners are pof-cli-prompt and pof-cli-terminal-ready. The button (src/components/cli/TerminalOutput/SelectionToolbar.tsx, title 'Search in project') has been a no-op since it landed (bc20b505). Two honest fixes: wire it to an existing search surface (direction: which one) or remove the button.

## Flow
- select text in the terminal -> toolbar -> Search
- event dispatched, 0 listeners
- selection cleared, nothing searched

## Expected impact
The toolbar stops offering an action it cannot perform. Removing it changes the visible toolbar; wiring it needs a search target chosen.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every toolbar button does what it says
Before: 1/3 toolbar buttons is a no-op (0 listeners)
After: remove: 0/2 no-ops; wire: 0/3
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep over src and e2e
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep -rn pof-terminal-search src e2e -> src/components/cli/TerminalOutput/useTerminalOutput.ts (dispatch only)
window listeners: 'pof-cli-prompt' x2, 'pof-cli-terminal-ready' x1

title: Context 'knowledge-system' holds only the localization pipeline store
body:
## Summary
The context named knowledge-system contains two files, both the localization pipeline (store + types); no knowledge-system code is in it, and its registry row is governance 'weak'.

## Description
context-map.json lists only src/stores/localizationPipelineStore.ts and src/types/localization-pipeline.ts for knowledge-system; .ai/registry-map.json maps it to knowledge-registry / agent-memory / engine-pitfall-corpus etc., none of which these files touch. The real localization surface (src/components/modules/evaluator/LocalizationPipelineView/**, src/lib/localization/**, src/app/api/localization-pipeline) sits elsewhere, so sweeps of this context judge a store against the wrong subjects. Fixed = rename/merge into the localization context, or move the knowledge files (src/lib/knowledge/**) into it - a context-map edit.

## Flow
- read context-map.json knowledge-system file_paths
- 2/2 files are localization
- registry subjects matched: 0 applicable

## Expected impact
Future sweeps and registry conformance judge these files against the right subjects. Changes the context map (operator-owned).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - context scope matches its name
Before: 2/2 files off-topic for the context name; 6 registry subjects, 0 applicable
After: predicted: 0 off-topic files
Method: probe - read of context-map.json and registry-map row
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
context-map.json knowledge-system.file_paths = [src/stores/localizationPipelineStore.ts, src/types/localization-pipeline.ts]
.ai/registry-map.json knowledge-system governance: weak
